title: One visit counter for the whole website
hints: How many VisitCounter objects exist while the website runs? How many should there be, so that every page adds to the same total?
Let the VisitCounter class itself keep the one counter and hand it out to anybody who asks. Nobody else should be allowed to build another one.

quiz.question: Look at how HomePage and AboutPage get their VisitCounter. Which principle does this code break most clearly?
quiz.explanation: Each page runs `new VisitCounter()` itself, so every page decides how many counters exist. Nobody is in charge of "there should only be one": that job is scattered over the pages, which is Single Responsibility, and the pages also depend on how a counter gets built instead of being handed the one they should use, which is Dependency Inversion. Either answer is accepted. The visible damage: Home counts its own visits, About counts its own, and nobody can say how many visits the website really had.

steps.title: Keep one counter inside VisitCounter
Use the shared counter in both pages
steps.md:
Now make the pages use it. In `HomePage.java` and in `AboutPage.java`, find the line that says `new VisitCounter()` and replace it with `VisitCounter.getInstance()`.

That is the only change. After it, Home and About add to the same counter, so both can tell the real total. Press **Check step 2**.

steps.title: Stop anyone from making another counter
steps.md:
As long as `new VisitCounter()` is allowed, somebody can still make a second counter by accident. Close that door: add a **private constructor** to `VisitCounter.java`.

```java
private VisitCounter() { }
```

Now only `VisitCounter` itself can create a counter, and everybody else has to ask `getInstance()`. The pages already do, so nothing else changes. Press **Check step 3**. When all three steps pass, press **Submit** to see what you built.

roles.name: Singleton (the one shared object)
roles.is: VisitCounter, with its private constructor, the static instance field and getInstance()

roles.name: Clients (the users of the shared object)
roles.is: HomePage, AboutPage, and the ContactPage that the tests define

reveal.summary: Singleton makes sure a class has exactly one object and gives everybody the same way to reach it, so every page adds to one shared counter instead of keeping a private one. Do not use it by reflex: it is hidden global state that any class can change from anywhere, and tests that depend on it can affect each other. When only a few classes need the object, prefer creating it once and passing it to them, so the dependency is visible.
